title: Lockstep simulation of a choice prefix
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x,y$ be finite binary words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $N$ on input $x$. Suppose a Boolean tag $b$ satisfies the virtual boundary-tag condition for the input-head position of $c$. For every finite binary word $u$, natural number $t\le |u|$, and physical input position for $y$, there is a Boolean tag $b'$ such that the run of $N$ from $c$ under the first $t$ bits of $u$ has a valid boundary tag $b'$, and the simulation core run for $t$ steps from the encoding of $c,b,u$, choice-head position $0$, and the given physical position equals the encoding of that resulting configuration, $b'$, $u$, choice-head position $t$, and the same physical position.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet
A Boolean tag satisfying the boundary condition for $c$'s input-head position
A physical input position among the positions for $y$
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let a configuration of $N$ on input $x$ carry a valid virtual boundary tag, and let $u$ be a choice word with $t \le |u|$. Then $t$ physical steps of the simulation core of $N$ carry the embedded configuration to the embedding of the run of $N$ under the first $t$ bits of $u$, again with a valid boundary tag.
